work.headingAccent: From the pile you hate to a row your accountant signs.
work.s1Title: Send us a month of the documents you hate
work.s1Desc: The crumpled ones. The phone photos taken at an angle. The bank statement PDF that is really a scan of a printout. Do not send us the clean ones, they prove nothing.
work.s2Title: We measure accuracy on YOUR documents
work.s2Desc: Not a percentage from a brochure. Yours, on your paper, and we show you the failures alongside the successes. Nobody on earth publishes a Georgian benchmark, so we are going to make one, and it will be yours.
work.s3Desc: Your chart of accounts, your VAT treatment, your supplier names as they are actually spelled in your books rather than as they appear on the invoice. This is the work that makes the rest of it boring.
work.s4Desc: You forward it or you drop it in a folder. There is nothing to install and nothing for your bookkeepers to learn. Low-confidence fields are held back for a human, and we tell you which they were.
work.s5Title: You get a file that imports
work.s5Desc: Not a JSON dump and not a CSV you have to re-map every month. A posted row, in the format your system already eats. The row is the product.
work.s6Desc: We produce a draft entry. He signs it. That is written into the contract, because we are not taking on your tax liability and any vendor who says they will is lying to you about something.

faq.subtitle: Beginning with the one that should make you suspicious of us.
faq.q1: My invoices are already in rs.ge. Why would I pay <brand></brand> anything?
faq.a1: For those, you should not. Georgia made electronic tax invoicing mandatory, so your domestic invoices and waybills are already structured data sitting in rs.ge, and any vendor selling you OCR for them is selling you a solved problem and hoping you have not noticed. The pile that is still manual is everything rs.ge does not contain: bank statement PDFs from BOG and TBC, foreign supplier invoices on imports, customs paperwork, and the photographs of fiscal receipts your clients send you for expense claims. That is the whole product. There is a sorter further down this page that tells you which of your own documents you should not be buying from us.
faq.a2: We do not know, and neither does anyone else, and that is the honest answer. There is no published Georgian-language document-extraction benchmark from any vendor on the planet. The 99% figures everyone quotes are English-document numbers on English invoices, and repeating them at you would be a lie by omission. So we measure it on your documents, before you pay, and that number is the one we both work from afterwards. If it comes back badly, we will tell you and you will have lost nothing.
faq.q3: Does it read Georgian Mkhedruli, or only English and Russian?
faq.a3: Printed Mkhedruli, yes. It is the photographed, angled, creased, thermal-printed receipt that decides whether this works for you, and that is exactly what we want in the pilot pile.
faq.a4: No. Not reliably, not in Georgian, not by us and not by anyone selling you something this year. If your pile is mostly handwritten, we are the wrong purchase and we would rather say that now.
faq.q5: What happens when it gets a number wrong? Who catches it?
faq.a5: The system does, most of the time, because it knows when it is unsure and holds that field back rather than guessing. A human sees the amber ones. The point of the confidence score is not to look clever, it is to make sure a wrong number never quietly becomes a posted row.
faq.q6: Do you integrate with ORIS, Balance or 1C?
faq.a6: We produce a file those systems import. Whether we can go further and post directly depends on your installation, and we will look at yours before promising anything, because the ones customised by a contractor who has since disappeared are a genre of their own.
faq.q7: Do I have to change my accounting software?
faq.a7: No, and if a vendor tells you that you do, he is selling you his software and calling it document processing. We fit around what you run.
faq.q8: What does it cost per document, and what if I only have 300 a month?
faq.a8: It is priced per document per client company, and 300 a month is small enough that you should think carefully about whether this is worth it at all. We will do that arithmetic with you honestly, because a bookkeeping firm with twenty client companies and eight thousand documents is a customer and a firm with three hundred documents is probably not, yet.
faq.q9: Where are my documents stored? Do they leave Georgia?
faq.a9: We will tell you plainly where they sit and what leaves the country, and we can run the whole thing on your own server if the Personal Data Protection Service is a conversation you would rather have once and never again. This is a normal request from an accounting firm and it should be.
faq.q10: Can it read a phone photo, or do I need a scanner?
faq.a10: A phone photo, yes, and that is most of what actually arrives. There is a section further down that shows you the same document as a clean scan, an angled phone photo, a crumpled thermal receipt, and a handwritten note, with the real output for each, including the one where it fails.
faq.q11: What happens when a supplier changes their invoice layout?
faq.a11: It usually keeps working, because it is reading meaning rather than pixel positions. When it does not, we fix the mapping and you are not billed for it, because a layout change is our problem to absorb and not a reason to send you an invoice.
faq.q12: My accountant is already fast. Prove you are faster.
faq.a12: We will not, on this page. Send us a month of his real work, we will run it, and we will show you both his time and ours on the same pile. If he wins, he wins, and you will have learned something useful about your own firm for free.
faq.q13: Can it handle customs declarations and import paperwork?
faq.a13: Yes, and for a customs broker or a freight forwarder that is usually where the volume and the pain actually are. Georgia is a transit corridor. Declarations, CMRs, packing lists and certificates of origin are a real pile and nobody has automated them here.
faq.q14: If the AI misreads a figure and I underpay VAT, who is responsible?
faq.a14: Your accountant signs the entry, so your accountant is responsible, and that is written into the contract in plain language. We produce a draft. We check our own accuracy and we hold back what we are unsure of. But a vendor who offers to carry your tax liability is either lying or has not read the law, and either way you should not sign with him.

row.eyebrow: Watch a receipt become a row
row.heading: This is the whole product, in nine seconds.
row.subtitle: OCR is a commodity. Anyone can buy the engine. What you are paying for is the last step, and everybody else stops one step short of it.
row.note: One row. That is what nine seconds of machine time buys, and it is the thing your bookkeeper was doing by hand.
row.commodity: Raw text OCR costs about 1.50 dollars per 1,000 pages from Amazon. That is the part everyone sells you. The row is the part nobody does.

split.eyebrow: The half you should not pay us for
split.heading: Sort your own pile. We will tell you where we are useless.
split.subtitle: Drag each document to where it belongs. Most vendors would rather you did not know this.
split.free: Already structured. Pull it from rs.ge, free.
split.e1: Mandatory in rs.ge. It is already structured data and it is already yours.
split.e2: Mandatory in rs.ge. Same. Do not pay anyone to read it.
split.e3: rs.ge has never seen this. It is a PDF and someone re-types it every month.
split.e4: An import. rs.ge has no idea this exists.
split.e5: Nobody has automated this in Georgia. It is a real pile and it is real money.
split.e6: A photograph, taken at an angle, of a thermal receipt that is already fading.
split.e7: rs.ge has never seen this either.
split.e8: Not in rs.ge, and the clauses that matter are prose, not fields.
split.outro: Half your pile is already free. We only want the other half, and now you know which half that is.

scans.heading: The same receipt, four ways. One of them defeats us.
scans.subtitle: Every vendor shows you the clean scan. Here is what actually arrives in your inbox.
scans.s1r: Every field read. Nothing held back.
scans.s2r: Every field read. The total was held back for a human, because the glare crossed it.
scans.s3r: Supplier and total read. Two line items held back. This is normal and it is why a human is in the loop.
scans.s4r: We cannot read this. Not reliably, not in Georgian, not this year, and not by anyone selling you something today.
scans.note: We are showing you the failure on purpose. A vendor who only shows you the clean scan is telling you what will happen in the demo, not what will happen in March.

proof.note: One posted row. That is the product, and it is the step everybody else stops one short of.
